--- title: "[Graph.add_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add an edge between two existing nodes in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1289-L1483){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_edge( source, target=None, rel=None, weight=None, auto_create_nodes=False, **attributes, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add edge](/assets/graphs/add-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: four nodes joined by three edges, C to A to B to D. After: a new edge between the existing nodes C and D, in the accent color, closes the cycle; no nodes are added." width="100%"} Edges connect existing nodes and can optionally carry weights and attributes. Both source and target nodes must already exist in the graph. You can reference nodes by their integer IDs or string labels (if labels are unique). Each call creates a new edge with its own auto-assigned edge ID, even if an edge between the same two nodes already exists, so calling it twice for the same pair produces parallel edges (a multigraph). Self-loops (`source` equal to `target`) are also allowed. Use `remove_duplicate_edges()`, `remove_selfloops()` or `simplify()` afterward if you need a simple graph. In a directed graph the edge points from `source=` to `target=`; in an undirected graph the order of the two endpoints doesn't matter. The graph is modified in place and the call is recorded in the step log (see `steps`). For adding many edges at once, `add_edges()` is more concise, and `add_edge_by_id()` is a strict variant that only accepts integer IDs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, rust.Edge]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The source node identifier: an integer is treated as a node ID and a string as a node label. In a directed graph this is the node the edge starts from. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The target node identifier (ID or label, resolved the same way as `source=`). In a directed graph this is the node the edge points to. Although it has a default of `None`, a target is required for normal use. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional string relationship type for the edge (e.g., `"friend"`, `"follows"`, `"manages"`). This is a first-class attribute that always appears as the fourth column in edge DataFrames (null when not set). Default is `None`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional numeric edge weight, such as a cost, distance or strength. The value is stored on the edge whenever it is given (and shown in a `weight` column of the edge DataFrame), independently of whether the graph was created with `weighted=True`. Default is `None` (no weight). [auto_create_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, any string label that doesn't match an existing node causes a new node with that label to be created first. Integer IDs are never auto-created. If `False` (default), all referenced nodes must already exist. [**attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Arbitrary key-value pairs to store as edge attributes (e.g., `since=2020`). Each key becomes a column in the edge DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target node doesn't exist in the graph, or if a label cannot be resolved to a node ID (and `auto_create_nodes=` is `False`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Nodes can be referenced by the IDs returned when they were created: ::: {#39ae08d4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="Alice") graph.add_node(label="Bob") alice_id = graph.get_id_from_label(label="Alice") bob_id = graph.get_id_from_label(label="Bob") graph.add_edge(source=alice_id, target=bob_id) graph.has_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: If labels are unique, it's usually simpler to reference nodes by label directly. Since `add_edge()` also returns `self`, the whole graph can be assembled in one chain, and IDs and labels can be mixed freely: ::: {#59501fbb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Carol") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") .add_edge(source=2, target="Carol") # node ID 2 is Bob ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 4)
idsourcetargetrel
i64i64i64null
112null
223null
``` ::: ::: `weight=` stores a numeric cost or strength, `rel=` labels the kind of relationship the edge represents, and any other keyword arguments become additional edge attributes. Each ends up in its own column of the edge DataFrame: ::: {#a518232a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob", rel="friend", weight=0.75, since=2020) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (1, 6)
idsourcetargetrelsinceweight
i64i64i64stri64f64
112"friend"20200.75
``` ::: ::: With `auto_create_nodes=True`, unknown labels are turned into new nodes, so a graph can be built from edges alone: ::: {#3df4db07 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_edge("Alice", "Bob", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("Bob", "Carol", auto_create_nodes=True) ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: ::: Adding the same pair twice doesn't overwrite the first edge; it creates a parallel edge with its own ID: ::: {#e2a00133 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B", rel="email") .add_edge("A", "B", rel="phone") ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
